title: Greg Doucette & MPMD Did Nothing Wrong™
summary: Playing ironic defense lawyer, NH argues Greg Doucette and Derek (More Plates More Dates) did nothing wrong selling turkesterone that tested as nearly empty, since turk does nothing even when pure. The real culprits are the gullible buyers and fanboys, plus the supplement industry behind them. Call-out videos change nothing, and the only fix is to stop buying supplements from fitness youtubers.
claims: Greg Doucette and Derek of MPMD sold turkesterone that independent testing found to contain barely any turkesterone
Turkesterone does nothing even in pure form, so buyers lost nothing extra; the anger targets the wrong issue
Buyers of bunk turk scammed themselves by trying to dodge hard work; most were novices with no gains
Both sellers openly use steroids, so buying a muscle-building supplement from them makes no sense
Derek repeatedly said his supplements might only work for hyper-responders and do nothing for most people
The goal of most youtube fitness is to grow a channel and sell out; there is no integrity or accountability, e.g. AthleanX faced no consequences after being caught using fake weights
Call-out videos change nothing: small youtubers wait for a big one to slip, farm views, and the cycle repeats
Fanboys run on emotion, not logic; supplement marketing exploits fear of missing out and insecurities about manliness
Both channels turned into infomercials, essentially newsletters for products; he stopped watching once that began
He estimates 70-80% of buyers were teenagers spending their parents' money; someone on minimum wage would not spend 80 dollars on a bottle
Big channels act as gatekeepers and natural selection; novices are supposed to realize they learn nothing there and graduate to better channels
The supplement industry is the real system; individual sellers are replaceable heads of a hydra
As with McDonald's and obesity, change comes from targeting the buyers, not the seller
Community testimonials like '+25 lb on my bench from Gorilla Mode turk' did more damage than Derek himself through social proof
Greg takes far more blame than Derek even though Derek pushed turk longer and sold more, because Derek still has a loyal fanboy base
The placebo defense fails: whatever effect buyers felt came from training harder, and they could have had it without the product
Saying Derek did not scam on purpose is worse: a supplement seller who does not check suppliers could just as easily sell something overdosed and toxic
A new magic muscle supplement will appear within 6-12 months and people will fall for it again
The only real fix is to stop buying supplements and products from fitness youtubers altogether
Serious lifters do not watch such channels; their audiences are tourists of lifting rather than citizens
